recaps.title: Market close
recaps.intro: Stocks fell broadly as chip names sold off ahead of Nvidia earnings and a string of tech outages rattled traders. After the bell, Nvidia beat on results and guidance in its first report since Jensen Huang's exit.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Dow drops 848.75 points, or 1.64 percent, to 50,759.42; S&P 500 falls 1.03 percent to its lowest close since late July; Nasdaq slips 0.74 percent
bullets.note: Chip stocks sold off before Nvidia results, and a report of an NSA network outage added to jitters, CNBC says. The VIX rose for a fourth day.

bullets.text: Apple says a service outage was caused by an internal update, not a cyberattack
bullets.note: Bloomberg says Apple is working to restore systems after the update caused wide-scale outages.

bullets.text: Nvidia beats on profit and revenue and guides above estimates in its first report since Huang's exit
bullets.note: Adjusted EPS was 2.68 dollars on 115.84 billion dollars in revenue; Nvidia sees about 130 billion dollars this quarter versus 125.1 billion expected, CNBC says.

bullets.text: Nvidia shares jump 2 percent after hours on another record quarter, with sales more than doubling
bullets.note: Data center revenue was 107.6 billion dollars versus 101.87 billion expected.

bullets.text: Nvidia's board approves a 150 billion dollar boost to its share buyback
bullets.note: Announced alongside third-quarter results after the close.

bullets.text: Former CEO Jensen Huang says he has received an outpouring of support calling for his return to Nvidia
bullets.note: CNBC says Huang would be open to returning if the board thought it in shareholders' best interest. Nvidia shares ended the regular session 0.5 percent lower.

bullets.text: The SEC is investigating Nvidia in the wake of the Huang scandal, the WSJ reports
bullets.note: The civil probe is looking at whether Nvidia violated investor disclosure laws, according to the WSJ.

bullets.text: The 10-year Treasury yield nears its longest stretch above 5 percent in nearly two decades
bullets.note: Investors are bracing for more Fed rate hikes, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Homebuilder sentiment drops to its lowest level in 14 years
bullets.note: Higher mortgage rates, rising costs and weaker consumer confidence led more builders to cut prices, CNBC says.

bullets.text: Bitcoin trades near 64,500 dollars after plunging roughly 50 percent, with about half of circulating coins underwater
bullets.note: Investors are shifting attention to the Anthropic IPO, citing Glassnode data.

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: Washington spent the morning on the Nvidia scandal and an alleged Iranian plot, while Democrats sorted out leadership and early 2028 and 2027 races took shape.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agrees to answer questions from House lawmakers on Dec. 1
bullets.note: He agreed under the threat of a subpoena, CBS says, after resigning as CEO last week.

bullets.text: Commerce and Justice release details of their criminal probe into Nvidia-linked Megaspeed
bullets.note: The Commerce Department began investigating the company in 2024, the Post says.

bullets.text: Trump warns Iran of unprecedented consequences over a reported dirty bomb plot targeting Washington
bullets.note: The CNN report cites unnamed US officials; Iran denies it and the White House says there is no credible threat.

bullets.text: Fed Governor Lisa Cook refuses to take part in a White House hearing on Trump's bid to fire her
bullets.note: She describes the process as unfair, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Trump brushes off the recent mass outages that hit air travel, banks and email, saying it's life
bullets.note: A US official separately said the tech woes were not tied to cyberattacks, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Congressional Democrats prepare to examine a 100 billion dollar Venezuela oil-field deal
bullets.note: The administration deal is with a controversial Venezuelan businessman to control more than a dozen oil fields, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Brazilian police probe whether a Vance co-founded donor network meddled in Brazil's election
bullets.note: The question is whether Rockbridge Network intervened illegally to aid Flavio Bolsonaro, a senior security officer told the Post.

bullets.text: Sen. Martin Heinrich is undecided on whom to back for Senate majority leader
bullets.note: He says he wants to hear from the party's new members before deciding.

bullets.text: Vance says he will decide sometime next year whether to run for president in 2028
bullets.note: Several close allies told the Post he is more likely to run than not.

bullets.text: Rep. James Comer announces a run for governor of Kentucky
bullets.note: He aims to flip the governor's mansion from Democratic to Republican control in 2027.

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Trump worked through the Quad and ASEAN in Manila as the Iran war simmered in the Gulf. Europe dealt with Ukraine funding, strikes in France and new parliaments in Serbia and Israel.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump and Thailand's prime minister sign a joint trade statement in Manila
bullets.note: They say the formal agreement will be finalized in the coming weeks, ABC says.

bullets.text: Trump says the US, India, Japan and Australia struck several critical minerals agreements
bullets.note: The deals aim to secure supply chains and reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.

bullets.text: The US and Mexico officially lose their measles-free status, international health officials say
bullets.note: A formal decision after this morning's reports, now covering Mexico as well.

bullets.text: Iran claims a third strike on US radar systems in Bahrain in less than a week
bullets.note: Authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted, CBS says.

bullets.text: Residents of Iran's Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz report several explosions, Fars says
bullets.note: Smoke was also seen over the island, the Iranian agency reported.

bullets.text: Qatar meets Iranian officials as it tries to mediate the war
bullets.note: Doha says the talks seek to bridge differences over current proposals and urges all sides to avoid escalation.

bullets.text: The EU will propose a new loan package for Ukraine on Wednesday
bullets.note: Some capitals still balk at the funding, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Ukraine reports drone strikes on two refineries deep inside Russia
bullets.note: It is the latest assault on Russia's oil-processing industry.

bullets.text: Israeli parties seeking to oust Netanyahu are set to vote in a new parliament speaker
bullets.note: A new speaker could help repeal some of Netanyahu's core legislation, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Serbia's new parliament meets for the first time after a student-led movement won the most votes
bullets.note: The Oct. 25 vote upended Belgrade's political landscape.

bullets.text: Public sector workers strike across France for pay rises
bullets.note: Demonstrations continue despite government efforts to ease tensions, AFP says.

bullets.text: Thousands in Haiti's capital cheer El Salvador's President Bukele and Salvadoran troops fighting gangs
bullets.note: Salvadoran forces are helping fight gangs in Haiti.

recaps.title: Market open
recaps.intro: Tech futures firmed as the AI selloff eased ahead of Nvidia earnings after the close. Retail sales beat underneath the headline, yields rose, and Disney and Home Depot reported before the bell.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Nasdaq 100 futures rise before the bell as the AI selloff eases ahead of Nvidia results
bullets.note: Bloomberg says investors are preparing for an all-important earnings release from Nvidia.

bullets.text: Nvidia reports after the close, its first earnings since Jensen Huang's ouster
bullets.note: Nvidia has lost 2 trillion dollars in value since its October peak, CNBC says.

bullets.text: October retail sales rise 0.2 percent; the control group gains 0.6 percent versus 0.3 percent expected
bullets.note: Sales excluding autos rose 0.6 percent, above the 0.4 percent estimate.

bullets.text: October industrial production falls 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent gain expected
bullets.note: Manufacturing output rose 0.3 percent; capacity utilization slipped to 76.4 percent.

bullets.text: Treasury yields rise after the economic data, with the 10-year near 5.14 percent
bullets.note: The two-year yield rose about 2.4 basis points to about 4.85 percent.

bullets.text: Fed's Musalem says several rate hikes are likely needed before spring
bullets.note: He sees a meaningful risk that high inflation will persist.

bullets.text: Disney beats on earnings and revenue and targets 3 billion dollars in cost savings by fiscal 2029
bullets.note: Adjusted EPS was 1.77 dollars on 25.95 billion dollars in revenue; shares rose nearly 2 percent early, CNBC says.

bullets.text: Home Depot names CFO Richard McPhail CEO, replacing Ted Decker next week, as it reports third-quarter results
bullets.note: Shares were down nearly 2 percent early; Decker, on medical leave since August, stays chairman, CNBC says.

bullets.text: Data center and photonics stocks rally on a report the US plans to block Chinese data center equipment imports
bullets.note: Coherent rose 11 percent and Applied Optoelectronics 8.6 percent, CNBC says, citing a Reuters report.

bullets.text: Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above the current 70 to 78 dollar range, CNBC reports
bullets.note: Bloomberg says Anthropic is guiding investors to the top of the range or above.

bullets.text: Emerging-market stocks slump to a seven-month low as the tech selloff extends
bullets.note: Investors are awaiting Nvidia earnings, Bloomberg says.

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Trump opened his Asia trip in the Philippines with a possible Kim Jong Un meeting floated, as Ukraine and Russia traded strikes on bridges. At home, the US formally lost its measles-elimination status and the Pentagon failed another audit.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump arrives in the Philippines to start an Asia swing that includes a summit with Putin and Xi later this week
bullets.note: CBS calls the summit with the Russian and Chinese leaders highly anticipated.

bullets.text: Trump says he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China this week
bullets.note: Reuters says a meeting could dramatically reshape his trip through East Asia.

bullets.text: Measles is no longer eliminated in the US
bullets.note: NBC calls it a reversal of one of the country's greatest public health achievements this century.

bullets.text: Ukraine strikes a major bridge linking Crimea to Russia for a second night as Russia hits two major Kyiv bridges
bullets.note: The fierce exchange of strikes targeted key crossings on both sides.

bullets.text: Vance says Trump will not let the Iran conflict become a forever war and is considering options to end it
bullets.note: It is a signal the administration is weighing ways out of the conflict.

bullets.text: Pentagon fails its ninth straight audit despite progress in organizing its finances
bullets.note: Bloomberg says the Pentagon is counting on Ernst and Young and AI tools to pass by fiscal 2028.

bullets.text: Transportation Secretary Duffy says it is still unclear why a router in Arkansas triggered last week's nationwide ground stop
bullets.note: The L3Harris-installed router set off a nearly five-hour nationwide aviation ground stop on Nov 13.

bullets.text: Mongolia's president says he will resign after facing corruption accusations
bullets.note: AP says the accusations came from a member of a faction of the ruling party.

bullets.text: Pope Leo says he is not planning to allow married Catholic priests for now
bullets.note: In his first comments on the idea, he said it is too divisive across the Church.

bullets.text: Deutsche Bank processed 582 million dollars of suspicious payments linked to Epstein, the FT reports
bullets.note: The report is based on leaked documents; the bank says the incidents date back many years.

bullets.text: Turkish authorities take pro-opposition Sozcu TV off air in a pre-dawn raid and appoint a trustee
bullets.note: It extends a crackdown on the opposition and renews media freedom concerns.

bullets.text: A Costa Rican journalist is shot dead, the first such killing in the country in 25 years
bullets.note: CBS reports the well-known journalist had reported death threats.

bullets.text: Canada and China extend trade deals as Xi meets Carney ahead of the APEC summit
bullets.note: Ottawa is seeking closer ties with Beijing amid strained relations with the US.

bullets.text: Drones account for nearly three-quarters of Sudan war deaths this year, the UN says
bullets.note: The UN figure shows how drones have come to dominate the war.

bullets.text: Police in Phoenix investigate a four-vehicle crash involving two driverless Waymo cars
bullets.note: Three people were taken to the hospital, one in critical condition, according to reports.

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Nvidia heads into earnings today under an interim CEO while new US chip curbs ripple through Asia and the company tightens export oversight. Anthropic's coming IPO is drawing valuation doubts as investors cool on AI stocks.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Nvidia faces an earnings test today under interim CEO Colette Kress after its stock dragged Wall Street into the red
bullets.note: Investors are more focused on who leads Nvidia after Jensen Huang's departure, Reuters says.

bullets.text: Nvidia forms a board committee to oversee national security and export control compliance
bullets.note: It comes after the US moved to cut off China's access to its powerful chips.

bullets.text: Nvidia warns chip buyers of possible US legal action tied to Chinese remote access to its AI chips, CNBC reports
bullets.note: New legislation on remote access could expose Nvidia and its customers.

bullets.text: US AI chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia's data center boom, and shares there tumble
bullets.note: The US is closing loopholes that let Chinese firms reach advanced AI chips via Southeast Asian data centers.

bullets.text: US releases details of its Megaspeed probe, saying the investigation began in 2024
bullets.note: Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud firm and Nvidia's Asia-Pacific partner.

bullets.text: Vance says the administration is concerned by reports a third country obtained Nvidia technology
bullets.note: He strongly defended the administration's export controls.

bullets.text: Reuters: China taps output from leading US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite
bullets.note: Chinese entities are using increasingly sophisticated methods, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Chinese envoy says chip equipment export curbs threaten the EU-China trade thaw
bullets.note: Chipmaking equipment is now a flashpoint in EU-China trade ties.

bullets.text: Australia's largest pension fund questions the valuation Anthropic is targeting in its IPO
bullets.note: The listing could be the biggest ever, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Fund managers slash exposure to technology stocks as optimism about the AI boom fades, a poll shows
bullets.note: Wall Street ended sharply lower Monday on AI jitters, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Meta faces a sanctions bid over withheld evidence in teen mental health cases
bullets.note: The bid centers on evidence Meta is accused of withholding.

bullets.text: Meta says it tuned Instagram to show less sexually suggestive and violent content in India
bullets.note: India's government is tightening oversight of online content.

bullets.text: California's consumer watchdog chief says AI companies that violate state rules will be taken to court
bullets.note: California's attorney general sued OpenAI on Monday.

bullets.text: Cassava Technologies seeks to raise up to 1 billion dollars to buy Nvidia chips for African AI data centers
bullets.note: It would expand AI computing capacity in Africa.

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: The Chargers finally won a game and the Magic handed the Celtics their first home loss. Alcaraz and Medvedev opened the ATP Finals with wins, setting up a Wednesday meeting.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Magic beat the Celtics 115-105, handing Boston its first home loss of the season
bullets.note: Orlando scored 40 points in the fourth quarter.

bullets.text: Joel Embiid scores 37, his first 30-point game of the season, as the 76ers win on the road
bullets.note: Philadelphia is No. 1 in the East after a third straight win.

bullets.text: Heat win their fifth straight behind a Giannis Antetokounmpo double-double
bullets.note: Miami rose to No. 4 in the East.

bullets.text: Jeremiah Fears, 20, becomes the youngest player in Pelicans history to record a triple-double
bullets.note: He broke the franchise mark set by Chris Paul in 2006.

bullets.text: Cam Boozer scores a career-high 29 as the Grizzlies beat AJ Dybantsa's team in DC
bullets.note: Memphis is 7-0 on the road and 10-4 overall.

bullets.text: Terrence Shannon Jr. sets a career high with 34 points as the Timberwolves win at home
bullets.note: Minnesota improved to 10-4.

bullets.text: Donovan Mitchell scores 39 to lead the Cavaliers to a home win
bullets.note: It was a game-high total.

bullets.text: Chargers beat the Ravens in Baltimore for their first win of the season
bullets.note: A late Baltimore fumble and a pass breakup sealed it.

bullets.text: Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson has a torn ACL, additional tests confirm
bullets.note: He will now focus on getting ready for 2027.

bullets.text: Packers still plan for Micah Parsons to return Nov 25 against the Rams
bullets.note: Matt LaFleur says Parsons has a couple more hurdles to clear.

bullets.text: Will Cuylle scores twice as the Rangers win on the 100th anniversary of their first game
bullets.note: The game opened the NHL's Original Six Series.

bullets.text: Carlos Alcaraz beats Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 to open his ATP Finals campaign
bullets.note: It is his 10th straight win; he is 43-5 this year.

bullets.text: Daniil Medvedev beats Flavio Cobolli 7-6, 6-3 at the ATP Finals
bullets.note: Alcaraz and Medvedev meet Wednesday in Group Lendl.

bullets.text: Arkansas State tells football coach Butch Jones he is out at the end of the year
bullets.note: He is 4-6 this season and 30-43 over six seasons.

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: Killington opens the ski season today as milder weather moves in. Barre mourned its mayor, Montpelier picked a police chief, and police in St. Albans and Burlington sought suspects.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Killington opens for the season Tuesday, the first resort in New England to open
bullets.note: First chair is at 10 a.m. at the latest and could be as early as 9.

bullets.text: Freezing fog clears this morning, with highs in the low to mid 50s
bullets.note: Temperatures keep rising starting today.

bullets.text: Barre City Mayor Thom Lauzon has died
bullets.note: The longtime mayor and developer was 65, Seven Days reports.

bullets.text: Montpelier picks Burlington Deputy Police Chief Jonathan Young as its new police chief
bullets.note: It ends a months-long search after the chief and deputy chief left in May.

bullets.text: Senate Democrats nominate Sen. Andrew Perchlik to be the next Vermont Senate president pro tempore
bullets.note: He won an uncontested caucus race after the party's sweeping election wins.

bullets.text: St. Albans police search for a carjacking suspect after a violent incident at Walmart
bullets.note: Police say not to approach the suspect and to call 911.

bullets.text: Burlington police search for a suspect in a weekend gunfire incident
bullets.note: Police are asking for the public's help.

bullets.text: Vermont State Police continue to investigate a suspicious death after a fire in Berkshire
bullets.note: A man's body was found outside a home after a car caught fire on the lawn.

bullets.text: A dismissed Bennington County murder case heads back to court
bullets.note: The suspect is already serving a federal prison sentence.
